golden.note: The product's own label 'Reparto o mansione' is a column of departments, read row by row. The hourly rate is never read.
One sheet per department: ONE table, and the sheet name is the department.
The title says RECEPTION; asking the person to confirm it is acceptable (tolerated), not required.
Two columns called Ore: which is planned and which is worked is the person's call.
'Ore previste' and its revision: which one is the plan is the person's call.
Real dates in the header and the title says the cells are planned hours.
Nothing says whether the hours in the cells are planned or worked.
Only Lun, Mar, Mer: the period in the title says which three days.
Mon..Sun and 'week 43' without a year: the week is the person's to name.
No date and no week anywhere, and nothing about the hours: both must be asked.
G1..G5: not recognisable as days of any week.
Hours per person for the whole week, no day: hours are never spread over days.
M/P/N/R/F are shift codes, not hours.
Start-end times, not a number of hours.
Abbreviations every hotel professional reads the same way.
MAN is manutenzione or management (direzione): it must be asked, never guessed.
Words that are not departments in any hotel's vocabulary.
Everyday department words of a hotel.
10/19..10/25: the day is above 12, so month-first is proved by the values.
03/10, 04/10, 03/11, 04/11: day-first or month-first cannot be proved.
19.10.2026 and 7,5: day-first is proved by the dots and the day above 12.
Two weeks stacked on one sheet (first table starts at row 3): which one to import is the person's call.
A three-line legend sits above the real table.
A hidden draft sheet holds a different, smaller table.
The summary sheet (per department, no days) comes first; the detail is the data.
'Ore da contratto' are contractual hours: they may or may not be the plan, so they must not be claimed as planned hours (nor is leaving them out an error).
'Turni Cucina' / 'Turni Sala': the sheet name carries the department.
No column holds hours.
One total per person: no day, no way to analyse day by day.
The TOTALE row does not add up the rows: the document contradicts itself.
'Reparto' holds people's names and 'Dipendente' holds departments: the headers contradict the values.
One column writes its dates two ways (19/10/2026 and 2026-10-19).
A blank template: header and no records.
A restaurant menu: not staff, bookings or costs.
A bookings export uploaded on the staff card.
Instruction-looking text in the title and a notes column: data, never obeyed.
Formulas as text, HTML, a right-to-left override and zero-width characters in a comments column: all of it is data.
A 24,000-character cell and a zero-width space inside 'Reparto'.
A table marked 'ESEMPIO ... NON MODIFICARE' (rows 3-4) with the same columns sits above the real one: the real one is the data; asking is fine.
A real department named 'Totale Qualità': its rows are records, not totals.
1,656 rows: a quarter of rosters for 18 people.
A bare 'Ore' in a roster: planned or worked is the person's call.
Monthly hours per person: no day, nothing to analyse day by day.

'Giorno' is the name of the weekday, 'Data' is the date.
The last three days are planned only: their actual hours are blank.
The department is given as each person's job title.
'Reparto: SPA E BENESSERE' written as a label and a value above the table.
Two weeks, one sheet each, the same columns: one table.
A four-line colour legend sits to the right of the first rows of the table.
Four tables with the same columns, each under its own department line and header: V3.0 cannot join them, so it must not import one and drop the rest silently.
Each department is written once in a cell merged over its rows.
An empty row between every two records.
'8 h', '7,5 ore': hours with their unit typed after them.
Overtime, leave and attendance %: numbers, but not planned or worked hours.
'Dal' and 'Al' next to a booking date and a channel: the stay's two dates.
No status / rooms column: a fixed value must be chosen by the person.

One sheet per month with the same columns: one table.
Confirmed and cancelled bookings in two tables with the same columns.
A modified booking is still a booking: which status it gets is the person's call.
'Telefono' and 'Email' are channels here, not contact data.
1.237,45 style: thousands with a dot, decimals with a comma.
'€ 330,00' and '330,00 €' in the same column.
Month-first dates with days above 12: proved by the values.
Every day and month is 12 or below: 03/04/2026 can be either.
Three columns, all called 'Data': which is which cannot be known.
'Total' is the only amount: it is the reservation's room revenue.
A printed report: a page-break line every 8 records.

Arrival plus nights: the departure is arithmetic NINFA does not do in V3.0.

A room-by-day calendar: occupancy marks, no bookings.

golden.note: 'TOTAL' / 'Totale' inside ordinary notes: those rows are bookings, not totals.
Planned and actual check-in side by side: which is the stay's arrival is a choice.
3,200 rows.
The arrival date is a line above each block; there is no booking id or booking date.
A front-desk list: no booking code and no booking date.
'ven 23/10/2026': the weekday abbreviation in front of the date.
Two months drawn side by side: a label above each block, every header twice.
Imponibile + IVA = Totale on every row.
On a third of the rows net + VAT is not the total: the document contradicts itself.
A bare 'Importo': net or gross is the person's call.
A bare 'Totale' is usually the gross amount: it must never become the net silently.
The only amount says it includes VAT: NINFA works with the net.
Energia, Lavanderia, Colazioni, Manutenzione, Pulizie, Software, Marketing, Altro.
Words no hotel vocabulary decides alone: the person says which category they mean.
03/04/2026, 05/02/2026...: day and month are both 12 or below.
1,234.56 with month-first dates (days above 12 prove it).
Credit notes (NC) carry negative amounts.
No currency anywhere: the hotel's own currency applies and is said on screen.
The same invoice number on several lines.
'Totale' / 'Subtotale' open an ordinary description: every row is an invoice line.
Two columns called Importo: one is the net and one the total, nothing says which.
The original and the adjusted net: which one counts is a choice.
A bank statement: movements, no supplier and no invoice number.
Payroll: personal and salary data, not a supplier register.
Staff on the costs card.
Bookings on the costs card.
A blank template.
One column writes its dates in two ways.
Received invoices and issued invoices with the same columns.
A hidden draft sheet holds other invoices with the same columns.
2,400 rows.
'Prot.' is the hotel's own protocol; the invoice number is the supplier's.
A payment schedule: no invoice date, no description.
The net is split into one column per VAT rate: no single net column exists.
A cash book: movements, no supplier and no invoice number.
Utility consumption: no supplier, no document number.
The supplier is the line above each block of invoices, not a column.
A category by month matrix: totals, not invoices.
